name: doip
scope_note: Raw TCP bytes, including the 8-byte DoIP header on every frame -- these vectors test the framing/addressing mechanics the header itself carries, not a complete UDS exchange, so nothing here goes through UdsTester. Needs xaloqi.tester.conformance.runner.DoipRawProbe (this package's one new, deliberately minimal transport primitive -- see this package's README for why a free, narrow raw-TCP-bytes probe is not the same gift as xaloqi-tester-pro's full DoipBus). Ported from EDS's own tests/unit_runnable/test_doip_conformance_vectors.c, itself an independent port of python-doipclient's test_client.py (MIT, Copyright (c) 2020 Jacob Schaer). No live dogfood target was run against in this pass -- EDS's own DoIP example (examples/basic_ecu_doip) is reachable over native_sim's internal loopback only, not from the host, without a separate zeth TAP bridge this pass did not build. Disclosed, not implied otherwise: this corpus's runner mechanics are unit-tested against a local test double (see tests/), which proves the comparison logic, not interoperability with any real DoIP stack.

vectors.name: default_activation_success
vectors.description: Routing Activation, Default type, success. Entity logical address 0x0001 matches upstream's own test_logical_address=1, used here for an exact end-to-end byte match on the full frame, not just the payload.

vectors.name: non_default_activation_denied
vectors.description: Routing Activation, non-Default type, denied. The RESPONSE bytes are upstream's own (test_failed_activation_constructor, client-decode side only); upstream's own suite pairs no specific request with this response, so the TRIGGERING request here is EDS's own (a non-zero activation type, the denial path EDS's doip_server.c implements) -- disclosed, not implied to be upstream's own request fixture.

steps.note: activation_type=0x01, the one EDS's own denial path implements

vectors.name: positive_ack_address_swap
vectors.description: Diagnostic Message -> positive ack, with source/target address swapped as ISO 13400-2 §7.8 requires (SA=the ECU that's acking, TA=the tester that sent the diagnostic message -- the opposite order from the request). The UDS data bytes in the request are arbitrary (no handler need be registered; only the ack that precedes dispatch is checked).

steps.note: setup: routing activation (response not asserted here)
drain the routing-activation response before the diagnostic exchange -- not asserted

vectors.name: positive_ack_address_swap_second_address
vectors.description: Same vector as VEC-DIAG-ACK-001, at a different ECU logical address -- an independent second data point that the SA/TA swap is not coincidental for one specific address pair.

steps.note: setup: routing activation against entity 0x1234 (response not asserted)
drain the routing-activation response -- not asserted
tgt=0x1234, a different ECU logical address than VEC-DIAG-ACK-001

vectors.name: request_response_byte_exact
vectors.description: Alive Check Request -> Response, full byte-exact match, payload included: the tester's own logical address, echoed from the routing activation beforehand (ISO 13400-2:2019 Table 28).

steps.note: drain the routing-activation response -- not asserted
Alive Check Response, payload = tester's own logical address
